answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may submit jobs or vote on reputation, then slash that bond when independent audits prove fraud. Creating a thousand sybils no longer means merely minting usernames: each must lock real capital, and coordinated accounts risk losing it together. The bond can grow with privileges, while a thread of linked activity helps auditors spot clusters; even at dawn, a meadow of fresh accounts must pay the same entry cost.
